detections.name: Epsilon Indi B
detections.note: Measured from these images, Epsilon Indi B drifts 4.41″ a year. The star catalogue gives 4.7″ a year. The two differ because the measurement also picks up parallax (Earth's own orbit) and some error in finding the star's centre.

notes: Two brown dwarfs, too close together for SPHEREx to separate. They move 4.7″ a year together with the star ε Indi A.
The crosshair shows where the star catalogue says the object should be on each date, given its motion of 4.7″ a year. Across these frames that is a shift of 1.1 pixels (6.8″).
